findings.text: Node creation validates the name strictly, allocates an inode with no-reserve mapping behavior, then applies access control setup and security initialization tolerating unsupported operation, registers a directory offset, grows the parent, refreshes parent times and version, and publishes the dentry persistently; any late failure releases the inode.

Temporary-file creation follows the same inode plus security plus access-control sequence but attaches the inode to the open file and completes through the simple-open finish path. Directory creation delegates to node creation with directory type and then increments the parent link count. Regular creation delegates with regular type.

Hard-link creation reserves inode space except when linking a previously unlinked temporary file, adds the new directory offset with rollback of the reservation on failure, grows the target directory and bumps its version. Unlink releases one reservation for multi-link non-directories, removes the offset, shrinks the directory, unlinks, and invalidates casefolded negative survivors where applicable.

Directory removal requires an empty victim, drops links on both victim and parent, then runs the common unlink path. Whiteout creation allocates a sibling dentry for the old name and creates a character special whiteout node there, releasing the temporary dentry reference afterwards.

Rename validates against the supported no-replace, exchange and whiteout mask. Exchange is delegated to the generic offset-exchange helper. Otherwise it requires an empty target, acquires a target offset where busy means already present, optionally creates a whiteout with rollback of a newly acquired offset, moves offsets, replaces a positive target with directory link-count repair, transfers abstract directory size between parents, and updates timestamps and versions on both parents.

Symbolic-link creation bounds total length including terminator by one page, allocates a link inode, initializes security tolerating unsupported operation, adds a directory offset, sets size to length without terminator, then branches: short targets duplicate the string and use cached-link operations, while longer targets use page-cache operations with a write folio that is filled, zero-padded, marked current and dirty, then unlocked and released. Failures remove the offset and release the inode.

Link resolution has a lock-free lookup path and a sleeping folio-acquisition path. Both reject hardware-poisoned folios and, respectively, non-current or absent folios with a retry-to-caller status. The sleeping path unlocks before returning. Success defers release to a callback that records access and drops the folio reference.

File attribute query exposes only the user-visible subset of stored flags. Update rejects extended attribute forms and any bit outside the user-modifiable set, preserves unmodifiable stored bits, delegates the effective flag change, stores the merged value on success, and updates change time and version.

When an inode limit is configured, bulk security-attribute installation and single-attribute updates pre-reserve abstract inode space under the superblock statistics lock and fail when insufficient. Successful replacement frees the old entry and refunds its space; unused or partially used reservations are refunded. Bulk installation prefixes names with the security namespace and reports allocation failure if the input list is not fully consumed.

Extended-attribute access resolves the handler-qualified full name and operates on the per-inode attribute list with a shared superblock cache. Listing enumerates that per-inode list into the caller buffer.

Export identity compares generation plus a 64-bit number split across two 32-bit words. Encoding requires a three-word buffer, lazily inserts unhashed inodes into the hash under a static lock using number plus generation as key, and emits generation plus low and high halves. Decoding validates length, reconstructs the number, looks up by number plus first word, and returns an existing alias. Parent lookup always reports stale.

Short and long symbolic-link operation tables share attribute and listing behavior and differ only in link resolver. The export table binds parent, encode and decode entry points. The attribute-handler table binds security, trusted and user prefixes to one shared get and set pair and is null terminated. Mount tables bind option names to an enum, huge-mode strings to constants, and typed parameter forms.

Directory size moves in fixed abstract entry units on create, link, unlink, rmdir and rename transfer, always paired with a version bump and usually a parent timestamp refresh. Link-count changes accompany directory creation, directory removal, and directory rename cases.

Filesystem statistics report a fixed type, page-sized blocks and maximum name length, expose block and file capacities only when superblock limits are set using a summed used-block counter and abstract free inode space, and derive the filesystem identifier from the superblock UUID. The observed allocation tail extends size only when keep-size is clear and the range end exceeds current size, clears the private pointer under the inode lock, and marks the file modified on success.

Mount parsing accepts size as bytes or percent of total RAM converted upward to pages, parses block and inode counts with trailing-text and range guards, masks mode to permission bits, requires uid and gid to be mappable, requires transparent huge-page support for non-never huge modes, restricts policy strings to NUMA builds, records inode-number width with a word-size guard for 64-bit mode, and restricts no-swap and quota forms to privileged initial-namespace contexts.

Casefold option handling has two build variants: one loads a Unicode map for the requested or latest UTF-8 version after validating the version prefix and reports load failures, while the other always rejects with unsupported-encoding status.

The inode lock guards clearing of the allocation private pointer. The superblock statistics lock guards all free inode-space reservation and refund updates. A static encode-time lock serializes the check-and-insert path that lazily hashes exportable inodes.

Poisoned or not-current link storage, absent link folio, overlong link target, unsupported rename flags, non-empty rename or rmdir victim, and exhausted attribute inode space each fail the operation rather than proceeding with inconsistent state.
Exported file handles use a three-word form carrying generation, low inode number and high inode number, with encode and decode both enforcing minimum length three.
Symbolic-link payloads are bounded by one page including terminator; short payloads use cached-link storage while longer payloads use page-cache folio storage.
Supported huge-mode mount strings are never, always, within_size and advise, mapped to distinct huge-policy constants.
